readme: The one place every Canopy keyboard shortcut is defined. Both the Rust
native menu (src-tauri/src/shortcuts.rs) and the webview key handlers
(src/shortcuts.ts) read this file, so a chord is written once and both
sides agree on every platform.
chord.mods uses abstract tokens, resolved per platform:
Mod   -> Command on macOS, Control on Windows/Linux (the primary key)
Ctrl  -> literal Control everywhere (the physical ^ key on a Mac)
Alt   -> Option on macOS, Alt elsewhere
Shift -> Shift
Meta  -> literal Command/Windows/Super. Never use in a default; it is
the OS's key on Windows and Linux.
chord.key is a KeyboardEvent.code (KeyN, Comma, ArrowLeft, PageDown), or
null for a modifier-only chord used with a mouse click.
platform holds per-OS overrides. A platform mapped to null is unbound
there. A platform not listed inherits chord.
keyLabel overrides how the key renders in the help table (a range like
"1…9"). A label may contain {mod} or {alt}, substituted with this
platform's spelling of that modifier. scoped:true means the chord is live
only while one surface has focus, so it may reuse a global chord.
Off macOS a chord may also move because plain Ctrl+<letter> is a readline
or termios binding the shell needs (Ctrl+K kill-line, Ctrl+W werase). Those
carry a note saying which. Canopy is terminal-first: a chord that silently
eats a shell key is worse than one the user has to learn.

vscode.label: VS Code
vscode.description: Familiar VS Code navigation and workbench shortcuts.

jetbrains.label: JetBrains
jetbrains.description: Navigation shortcuts shared by IntelliJ IDEA, WebStorm, PyCharm and other JetBrains IDEs.

sublime.label: Sublime Text
sublime.description: Goto Anything and command shortcuts from Sublime Text.

shortcuts.label: New tab — shell, preview or an agent (type to filter, ↵ to open)
Previous project
shortcuts.note: Ctrl+Alt+Arrow is screen rotation on Intel drivers (Windows) and workspace switching (GNOME/KDE), so the non-Mac binding moves to PageUp/PageDown — the same pair the tab chords use one level down.

shortcuts.label: Close project
shortcuts.note: The former Shift+Mod+W now closes a whole multiplexed tab; project close remains available from its title-bar pill.

shortcuts.label: Jump to a tab — hold {mod} to show tab numbers
shortcuts.note: A range, not one chord: useHeldModifier reads any Digit1..9 with this modifier. keyLabel is what the help table shows.

shortcuts.label: Jump to a project — hold {alt} and the pills show their numbers
New terminal in the active project
Split pane right and choose an agent
Split pane down and choose an agent
Previous tab
shortcuts.note: Mac keeps Ctrl+Cmd+Arrow. Off Mac that chord collapses to Ctrl+Arrow, which is word-jump in every text field, so tabs use the Ctrl+PageUp/PageDown pair browsers and VS Code already train.

shortcuts.label: Previous tab — hold Ctrl and the switcher stays up, with a live picture of each
shortcuts.note: Ctrl literal on every platform, not Mod: Ctrl+Tab is one chord worldwide, and Cmd+Tab belongs to the macOS app switcher. Deliberately surface "app" rather than "menu" — muda hands macOS the glyph U+21E5 as Tab's key equivalent rather than the character the key produces, so a menu item for it renders perfectly and never fires. ProjectView's capture-phase handler answers it, which is where it has to work anyway.

shortcuts.label: Next tab — hold Ctrl and the switcher stays up, with a live picture of each
Close tab
shortcuts.note: Off macOS Mod is Ctrl, and plain Ctrl+W is unix-word-rubout (and the terminal driver's own werase) in readline — a key the shell needs far more often than Canopy does. Ctrl+Shift is the namespace every terminal emulator already reserves for app commands (Windows Terminal and GNOME Terminal put copy/paste/new-tab there), and it keeps the letter, so the chord is the Mac one plus Shift.

shortcuts.label: Quick-open a file
shortcuts.note: Off macOS Mod is Ctrl, and plain Ctrl+P is previous-history in readline — a key the shell needs far more often than Canopy does. Ctrl+Shift is the namespace every terminal emulator already reserves for app commands (Windows Terminal and GNOME Terminal put copy/paste/new-tab there), and it keeps the letter, so the chord is the Mac one plus Shift.

shortcuts.label: SpotSearch — search everything, or run what you type as a task
shortcuts.note: Off macOS Mod is Ctrl, and plain Ctrl+K is kill-line in readline — a key the shell needs far more often than Canopy does. Ctrl+Shift is the namespace every terminal emulator already reserves for app commands (Windows Terminal and GNOME Terminal put copy/paste/new-tab there), and it keeps the letter, so the chord is the Mac one plus Shift.

shortcuts.label: Clipboard history — hold the modifiers, tap V to cycle, release to paste
shortcuts.note: Cmd+Shift+V is the familiar paste-history chord on macOS. Off macOS Ctrl+Shift+V belongs to terminal paste and Ctrl+Alt+V is the default dictation-history cycle, so clipboard history adds both Alt and Shift rather than stealing either existing paste path.

shortcuts.label: Toggle sidebar
shortcuts.note: Off macOS Mod is Ctrl, and plain Ctrl+B is backward-char — and the default tmux prefix in readline — a key the shell needs far more often than Canopy does. Ctrl+Shift is the namespace every terminal emulator already reserves for app commands (Windows Terminal and GNOME Terminal put copy/paste/new-tab there), and it keeps the letter, so the chord is the Mac one plus Shift.

shortcuts.label: Voice dictation — speak, press again to insert (Esc cancels)
shortcuts.note: Off Mac, Mod is Ctrl and plain Ctrl+D is shell EOF — it would close the terminal you were dictating into. This is the default only; Settings can rebind it.

shortcuts.label: Ask the companion — summon it, or put it away
shortcuts.note: Off macOS Mod is Ctrl, and Ctrl+/ is readline's undo — a key the shell needs far more often than Canopy does. Ctrl+Shift is the namespace terminal emulators already reserve for app commands, and it keeps the key, so the chord is the Mac one plus Shift.

shortcuts.label: Save the file you are editing
Submit the box you are typing in — commit message, agent comment, task brief
Newline inside a box that submits on Enter
Click a preview link to open it in your browser instead
shortcuts.note: Modifier-click, not a key chord. Strictly Cmd on macOS and Ctrl elsewhere: accepting either meant Ctrl-click on a Mac — which is the OS's right-click — silently opened the system browser.

shortcuts.label: Jump between Settings sections while Settings is open
shortcuts.note: Scoped: bound only while the Settings dialog is open, so it deliberately reuses tab-jump's chord.

shortcuts.label: Terminal: delete word
shortcuts.note: Documented, not implemented here — xterm.js itself sends ESC+DEL for this and readline binds it on every platform.

shortcuts.label: Terminal: start of line
shortcuts.note: macOS natural text editing, the iTerm2 mapping. Off Mac there is no Cmd key: Mod would resolve to Ctrl (Ctrl+Left is word-jump, not line-start) and the Super key belongs to the window manager. Home/End already do this on those platforms.
